strengths: The core direct-config surfaces are present and separated cleanly: Mulligan anchors compile into Mulligan.json, baseline-controlled posture compiles into GlobalValues.json, explicit card behavior compiles into per-card CardID files, and exact combo chains compile into Combo.json.

Hero Power handling is stronger than generic text matching. The repo has a dedicated hero-power behavior lane, explicit hero_power_transform support, linked-entity resolution for starting or replaced Hero Powers, and an explicit Imbue posture model.

Target and option handling is conservative in the correct way. Battlecry and hero-power targeting can lower into documented runtime blocks, while Discover and Choose One stay identity-gated so unresolved option identity is suppressed rather than guessed.
Generated entities are not flattened into fake generic value. Exact linked or resolved identities can participate in lowering, while random generated pools are kept warning-only.

Modern mechanics are explicitly named instead of silently falling through. Kindred, Tourist, Starship, Imbue, Rewind, Herald, Shatter, and future unknown mechanics all have a declared policy in the mechanic registry.

The no-block boundary is well documented and test-backed. Valid packages remain load-safe even when some mechanics are only partial or warning-only, which is the correct contract for a pre-run generator rather than a full strategy engine.
gaps: Dredge, Tradeable, Kindred, Tourist, Starship, Rewind, Herald, and Shatter are intentionally warning-only. That is the correct safety boundary, but it also means decks built around those mechanics receive visibility rather than rich action guidance.

Secret timing, repeated Location activation, generic spell targeting, and random generated-entity pools still sit outside the executable surface set. They are explained to the operator but not lowered directly.
Discover and Choose One richness still depends on source-backed option identity. When the option card cannot be resolved, the repo correctly suppresses lowering instead of approximating behavior.

Generated-entity handling is partial rather than closed-form. The system can link known entities and Hero Power transforms, but it does not fully close every random pool, transform chain, or future token ecosystem from static input alone.

Representative deck proof is thinner than registry proof for some newer mechanics. The repo has strong micro-tests and explicit registry coverage, but not every warning-only mechanic is demonstrated through a dedicated representative deck fixture.
no_block_assessment: Valid decks remain unblocked when the package is technically valid. The local operator contract explicitly allows load-safe apply for technical_status=VALID_PACKAGE even when mechanic visibility still contains partial or warning-only items.
Technical invalidity still blocks, and that is the right gate. Missing required runtime files or structurally invalid output should stop apply; semantic richness gaps should not.
The direct, identity-gated direct, partial, and warning-only split is the correct no-block model for this domain. It separates what the system can safely emit from what it should only describe.
Warning-only coverage is honest rather than weak. Dredge, Tradeable, Kindred, Tourist, Starship, Rewind, Herald, and Shatter stay visible and searchable without being promoted into fake runtime rows.
Unknown future mechanics also remain non-blocking by design. The fallback path is warning-only with registered=false, which prevents silent drift while keeping valid decks load-safe.
skill_slimness_assessment: The current HSConfig scope stays slim because it stops at pre-run package generation, semantic enrichment, and operator-facing explanation. It does not drift into post-run tuning or HSTuner-style runtime adaptation.
Most semantic breadth comes from a compact registry plus targeted enrichers and tests, not from a sprawling set of bespoke workflows. That is the right architecture for a lean pre-run system.
Keeping choice-heavy and state-heavy mechanics warning-only is a slimness strength. It avoids widening runtime writes or introducing speculative behavior just to claim broader coverage.
The compile layers are narrow and readable: Mulligan, GlobalValues, CardID, and Combo each have a single clear compiler surface. That keeps the system usable and auditable.

The main slimness risk would be proof sprawl, not product scope. The repo should prefer compact mechanic fixtures and drift tests over adding one representative deck or one operator branch for every new keyword.
hearthstone_coverage_assessment: Mulligan anchors, GlobalValues, CardID behavior, and Combo are covered at the right depth for direct config generation. They are explicit compilers, not inferred post-run behavior, and that is exactly what a pre-run generator needs.

Hero Power semantics are covered at the right depth. Normal Hero Power use has a dedicated behavior block, hero_power_transform is identity-gated direct, and Imbue is modeled as partial because it changes and upgrades Hero Powers but still depends on broader runtime state for exact sequencing.

Target and option semantics are covered conservatively. Documented battlecry and hero-power target rules can lower into direct runtime blocks, while Discover and Choose One only lower when exact option identity is known. Generic spell targeting stays warning-only, which is the correct boundary.

Generated entities are covered at the right depth for pre-run work. Known generated or linked identities can contribute to config generation, but random pools stay warning-only because the system should not invent exact pool semantics from static input alone.

Weapons are covered strongly and directly. Public Hearthstone rules treat weapons as hero-equipped attack and durability objects, and the repo maps them into play timing, physical attack posture, and exact combo sequencing when warranted.

Secrets and Locations are covered partially, which is the correct level. Playing a Secret or a Location can influence pre-run timing and posture, but hidden Secret trigger timing and repeated Location activations are separate stateful behaviors that remain warning-only.

Dredge and Tradeable are covered as visibility-only mechanics, and that is appropriate. Their defining value comes from out-of-hand or choice-before-resolution decisions that the current documented runtime rows do not express safely.

Kindred, Tourist, and Starship are also covered at the right level as warning-only. Kindred depends on previous-turn type or spell-school state, Tourist is primarily a deckbuilding identity rule, and Starship is a build-and-launch board object with accumulated pieces and a dedicated launch interaction.

Rewind, Herald, and Shatter should remain warning-only in a direct-config generator. Rewind depends on prior-outcome replay, Herald depends on card-specific Colossal soldier and scaling logic, and Shatter depends on split-hand recombination and follow-up state that go well beyond the current direct runtime surfaces.

Unknown mechanics are handled correctly. The system does not silently ignore future drift; it reports unregistered mechanics as warning-only, which is safer than blocking valid decks or inventing unsupported lowering.

Overall, the semantics are at the right level for direct config generation because the repo is trying to emit safe, loadable, evidence-shaped configs, not to simulate every gameplay decision tree. The remaining polish need is better proof density for a few boundaries, not a broader runtime surface set.
recommended_next_action: Add one compact mixed-mechanic regression fixture set that proves the current boundary for Discover or Choose One option identity, Secret timing, Location activation, and one text-only modern keyword such as Kindred or Rewind in a single operator-visible report wave, without widening runtime lowering.
